content.comment_body: Hello, I have a program saved on an SD card that was created using [product_name] [article_no] with firmware [version_no]. If I insert this SD card into a newer [product_name] [article_no] device with a different firmware version, the program won't load and instead initiates a restart, then displays 'Clear Program' on startup. The only method I've found to load the program is through [product_name] Comfort. Additionally, if an SD card is formatted with the new [article_no] device, it is incompatible with the older hardware. We deploy hundreds of machines annually using [product_name], and for future updates, we usually send an SD card update. I've always tracked which machine has which [product_name] version and kept one of each PLC for programming purposes, but now I need to monitor firmware versions and retain one of each [article_no] revision for each update?

Yes, tracking will be necessary, not necessarily for each firmware release but for every significant software update or upgrade. If new hardware appears in the selection list, it typically means a new firmware version is available.

Thank you for your reply. It's unfortunate that [product_name] now has compatibility issues, as previous versions did not have such problems in my experience. If certain versions like [article_no] Standard and FS4 are not compatible, it should be clearly indicated on the PLC hardware, or at least reflected in the Diagnostics menu for easier identification.
Actually, that's not the case. With new hardware, if you want a program designed for older devices to work, you must adapt the program to the new hardware specifications.

I've faced a similar issue, and it's not entirely clear how to resolve it from the previous discussions. What exactly do FS3 and FS4 mean for [article_no]? I need to be able to load a program onto any [article_no] device; I have one with firmware [version_no] that works, but the same SD card fails to load onto another unit with [version_no]. When attempting this, it briefly displays 'clear prog,' seems to load, but after pressing 'start,' it shows 'Error Empty Program.' I'm using [product_name] Comfort [version_no] on Windows 7, and updating the software or hardware results in varied error messages. See the attached error logs. A colleague also tried with Windows 10 and experienced identical issues. We've already returned an affected unit to our vendor, and the replacement shows the same problem. I'm hoping for a straightforward solution—please advise.

There are two distinct hardware versions of the [product_name] [article_no]. The older model is marked as Standard, with firmware versions ranging from [version_no] (FS01 to FS03 production statuses). The newer model, FS4, carries firmware [version_no] and production status FS04. Using [product_name] Soft Comfort [version_no], you can only create or edit programs for Standard hardware, not for the FS4 version. For FS4 devices, [product_name] Soft Comfort [version_no] is required. For detailed upgrading steps, reference the relevant discussion on upgrading from LSC V8.0 to V8.1. Note: Run the software as an Administrator during the upgrade.
Reopening the application as administrator resolved the issue. Much appreciated!

I've performed multiple updates and never encountered this problem, even when upgrading from [version_no] to [version_no]. Alternatively, you can download updates, drivers, or demo software from the official [company_name] website. Download the upgrade file (a Setup.exe) and execute it as an administrator.
Thank you—running the setup as administrator fixed the upgrade problem. I successfully loaded the program after changing the PLC type to the FS4 version. Thanks again!

A new question published by [user_name] has been moved to a separate thread titled 'Is it possible to create a file on an SD card to load into an older firmware version with [product_name] Soft Comfort [version_no] and new [product_name] hardware.' Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering significant compatibility problems when attempting to transfer programs between various hardware and firmware versions of the [product_name] [article_no] series. Programs developed for one version often cannot be loaded onto devices with a different hardware or firmware release, causing confusion, downtime, and additional tracking requirements. Migration to newer hardware necessitates the use of updated software ([product_name] Soft Comfort [version_no]), which adds complexity and increases the potential for failed updates and unexpected system errors such as 'Clear Program' and 'Error Empty Program.'
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect backward and forward compatibility across all hardware and firmware versions of the [product_name] [article_no] and its associated software. They want seamless program updates for their machines without the need to monitor minor hardware differences or manage multiple hardware and software revisions separately.
